title: 75-Day SDE Plan
subtitle: Modified 75 Hard for SDE interviews: DSA, HLD, LLD in C#, AWS then Azure, and daily habits

phases.name: Foundations
phases.summary: Arrays, windows, stacks, binary search, linked lists; OOP, SOLID, core patterns; scaling, databases, caching, queues; AWS core.

phases.name: Build and apply
phases.summary: Trees, heaps, graphs, tries, intervals; classic LLD problems; APIs, microservices, real-time; serverless, containers, deploys.

phases.name: Azure and interview mode
phases.summary: DP, backtracking, greedy, mixed sets; timed LLD mocks; HLD case studies; Azure mapped to AWS.

rules: 3 LeetCode a day: 2 in the morning, 1 at night. 30 minutes max per problem; if stuck, read the solution, mark it ↻ revisit and re-solve it on Sunday.
Floor vs full: on a drained day switch to Easy day - 3 easy LeetCode + 1 km walk + water + clean food + the HLD read still counts.
One theme a day: the HLD read, the LLD code and the cloud lab explain the same idea from three angles.
One cloud at a time: AWS for days 1–50, Azure for 51–75, each mapped to the AWS service you already know.
Cloud labs: always delete resources afterwards and keep a billing alarm on.
Never double up to catch up: missed tasks go to the catch-up list and get done on Saturday or Sunday.
Checkpoints on days 25, 50 and 75 have pass criteria - if one fails, repeat its weak topic before moving on.

weekday: Start the water count before the phone
Fresh brain, hardest problem first; 30 min max each
Fill a 1 L bottle for the desk
The day's office topic; read or watch
LLD 30 min + cloud 30 min, then LeetCode #3
Code the LLD in C#, then the cloud lab
saturday: Tie the week's HLD, LLD and cloud into one small project
sunday: Re-solve every ↻ revisit from the week first
45 min: revise the week on one page
Say each topic out loud in 2 sentences

habits.label: Water 2.5–3 L (1 L by lunch, 2 L by 7 pm)

easy_day: 3 LeetCode (the day's easiest, or Easy re-solves)

patterns.Arrays & hashing: Trade memory for time: a HashMap / HashSet turns an O(n^2) scan into O(n).
patterns.Two pointers: Sorted input or a palindrome? Move two indices toward each other instead of nesting loops.
patterns.Sliding window: Grow the right edge, shrink the left while the window breaks the rule; track the best window.
patterns.Stack: Anything 'nearest greater/smaller' or matching pairs is a monotonic or plain stack.
patterns.Binary search: Search the answer space, not just arrays: find the first value where a yes/no check flips.
patterns.Linked list: Draw it. Dummy head for edits, slow/fast pointers for middle and cycles, reverse in place.
patterns.Prefix sum: sum(i..j) = prefix[j+1] - prefix[i]; a HashMap of prefix counts finds subarrays with target sums.
patterns.Arrays & matrix: In-place tricks: reverse segments, swap by index, use the first row/column as markers.
patterns.Trees: Recursion returns what the parent needs; DFS for depth/paths, BFS (queue) for levels.
patterns.Heap / priority queue: Top-K or 'always the smallest next' = heap; keep it size K for O(n log K).
patterns.Graphs (BFS / DFS / union-find): Grid or adjacency list; BFS for shortest steps, DFS for components, topo sort for dependencies.
patterns.Trie: Each node = one character with children map + end flag; prefix queries become O(length).
patterns.Intervals: Sort by start (or end for greedy removal), then merge or compare neighbours.
patterns.Bit manipulation: x & (x-1) drops the lowest set bit; XOR cancels pairs; shifts read bits one by one.
patterns.Advanced graphs (Dijkstra / MST): Weighted shortest path = Dijkstra with a min-heap; connect-all-cheaply = Prim/Kruskal.
patterns.Dynamic programming: Define dp[i] in words, write the recurrence, fix the base case, then optimise space.
patterns.Backtracking: Choose → explore → un-choose; prune early; sort first when duplicates must be skipped.
patterns.Greedy: Prove the local choice never hurts (exchange argument) before trusting it.
patterns.Hashing: Map each item to a canonical key (sorted string, pattern, count signature) and compare keys.
patterns.Design data structures: Combine structures: HashMap for lookup + array/list for order or random access.
patterns.Math & strings: Handle signs, overflow and edge characters first; build results digit by digit.
patterns.Kadane / subarrays: Best subarray ending here = max(x, best_ending_prev + x); keep a running global best.
patterns.Mixed interview set (LeetCode 75): Name the pattern in the first 2 minutes, say the brute force, then optimise out loud.
